content_en:
AMD Zen 6 Preparations, Ryzen AI Halo LED Driver & Many Laptop Changes For Linux 7.3
The x86 platform driver changes are now in place for the Linux 7.3 kernel with additions for upcoming AMD Zen 6 hardware, the RGB LED driver controls for the Ryzen AI Halo PC, and a lot of laptop support additions and improvements for a variety of devices from different hardware vendors. Plus some handheld gaming device updates too.
Among the many x86 platform driver changes, the Ryzen AI Halo LED driver was merged for allowing the toggling of the LEDs and RGB control on the Ryzen AI Halo mini PC. It's a great and powerful Linux mini PC powered by Ryzen AI Max+. It even ships with its own in-house AMD Linux distribution too while now for Linux 7.3+ the mainline kernel can control the device's lighting configuration.
The AMD HSMP driver has also added protocol v7 support used by Zen 6 Family 1Ah Model 80H processors. There are also AMD PMF platform driver additions for Family 1Ah Model 80H processors, presumably the Zen 6 client desktop CPU models. The AMD PMF driver at large is also now exposing device metrics via a new ioctl interface.
The Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen2 AMD (20XL) also has an s2idle quirk within the AMD PMC driver.
On the handheld computer side, the MSI WMI driver added support for the MSI Claw's M Center keys.
The OneXPLayer "OXPEC" driver added support for the OneXPlayer X2 Mini Pro handheld.
Some of the other x86 platform driver updates include support for the ASUS ProArt PX13's "ProArt" key via the ASUS NB WMI driver. The ASUS Armoury driver also now supports adjusting power limits on more devices.
The LG laptop platform driver has added support for various events found on newer LG laptop models. The LG Gram 16T90SP also now has fixed keyboard backlight support.
The HP WMI driver for Linux 7.3 picked up GPU MUX switching support, supporting CPU and GPU PWM fan support independently, and new device support of the MEN MAX 16-ak0xxx, OMEN 16-n0xxx, OMEN 16-wd0xxx, OMEN 16-wf0xxx, OMEN board ID 8D88, and MEN Transcend 16-u0xxx support.
For Lenovo device support there is yb9-kbdock as a new driver for the Yoga Book 9 14IAH10. Also on the Lenovo device side for the ThinkPad APCI driver is support for the USB-C Security "USCS" feature on newer ThinkPads. USCS allows charging USB-C devices but data transfers are blocked.
The Samsung Galaxybook platform driver added support for the Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro.
For the Uniwill driver that is worked on a lot by TUXEDO Computers for their hardware, there is keyboard backlight, AC auto boot, and USB power-share support. The MACHENIKE L16 Pro, AiStone X4SP4NAL, and Avell A60 MUV laptops are now supported by that driver too.
Lastly the MSI EC driver added support for the MSI Raider A18 HX A9WJG and MSI Katana GF76 11UEK.
More details on the many x86 platform driver updates merged for Linux 7.3 can be found via this pull.

content_pt:
Preparações AMD Zen 6, driver Ryzen AI Halo LED e muitas alterações em laptops para Linux 7.3
As mudanças no driver da plataforma x86 estão agora em vigor para o kernel Linux 7.3 com adições para o próximo hardware AMD Zen 6, os controles do driver RGB LED para o PC Ryzen AI Halo e muitas adições e melhorias de suporte para laptop para uma variedade de dispositivos de diferentes fornecedores de hardware. Além de algumas atualizações de dispositivos de jogos portáteis.
Entre as muitas mudanças no driver da plataforma x86, o driver Ryzen AI Halo LED foi mesclado para permitir a alternância dos LEDs e do controle RGB no mini PC Ryzen AI Halo. É um excelente e poderoso mini PC Linux equipado com Ryzen AI Max +. Ele ainda vem com sua própria distribuição AMD Linux interna, enquanto agora para Linux 7.3+ o kernel principal pode controlar a configuração de iluminação do dispositivo.
O driver AMD HSMP também adicionou suporte ao protocolo v7 usado pelos processadores Zen 6 Family 1Ah Modelo 80H. Há também adições de driver de plataforma AMD PMF para processadores da família 1Ah modelo 80H, presumivelmente os modelos de CPU de desktop cliente Zen 6. O driver AMD PMF em geral também está expondo métricas de dispositivos por meio de uma nova interface ioctl.
O Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen2 AMD (20XL) também possui uma peculiaridade s2idle no driver AMD PMC.
No lado do computador portátil, o driver MSI WMI adicionou suporte para as teclas M Center do MSI Claw.
O driver OneXPLayer "OXPEC" adicionou suporte para o portátil OneXPlayer X2 Mini Pro.
Algumas das outras atualizações de driver da plataforma x86 incluem suporte para a chave “ProArt” do ASUS ProArt PX13 por meio do driver ASUS NB WMI. O driver ASUS Armory agora também suporta o ajuste dos limites de energia em mais dispositivos.
O driver da plataforma do laptop LG adicionou suporte para vários eventos encontrados nos modelos de laptop LG mais recentes. O LG Gram 16T90SP agora também possui suporte fixo para luz de fundo do teclado.
O driver HP WMI para Linux 7.3 adquiriu suporte para comutação GPU MUX, suporte para CPU e GPU PWM de forma independente e suporte para novos dispositivos MEN MAX 16-ak0xxx, OMEN 16-n0xxx, OMEN 16-wd0xxx, OMEN 16-wf0xxx, suporte para placa OMEN ID 8D88 e MEN Transcend 16-u0xxx.
Para suporte a dispositivos Lenovo, existe yb9-kbdock como um novo driver para o Yoga Book 9 14IAH10. Também no lado do dispositivo Lenovo para o driver ThinkPad APCI há suporte para o recurso USB-C Security "USCS" em ThinkPads mais recentes. O USCS permite carregar dispositivos USB-C, mas as transferências de dados são bloqueadas.
O driver da plataforma Samsung Galaxybook adicionou suporte para o Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro.
Para o driver Uniwill que é muito trabalhado pela TUXEDO Computers para seu hardware, há luz de fundo do teclado, inicialização automática AC e suporte para compartilhamento de energia USB. Os laptops MACHENIKE L16 Pro, AiStone X4SP4NAL e Avell A60 MUV agora também são suportados por esse driver.
Por último, o driver MSI EC adicionou suporte para MSI Raider A18 HX A9WJG e MSI Katana GF76 11UEK.
Mais detalhes sobre as muitas atualizações de driver da plataforma x86 mescladas para Linux 7.3 podem ser encontrados neste pull.

title_en: The "KVM Chainsaw" Clean-Up Merged For Linux 7.3 Along With Other Fixes
title_pt: A limpeza “KVM Chainsaw” mesclada para Linux 7.3 junto com outras correções
summary_en: The Kernel-based Virtual Machine "KVM" changes have landed for the Linux 7.3 merge window that is wrapping up later today...
summary_pt: The Kernel-based Virtual Machine "KVM" changes have landed for the Linux 7.3 merge window that is wrapping up later today...
content_en:
The "KVM Chainsaw" Clean-Up Merged For Linux 7.3 Along With Other Fixes
The Kernel-based Virtual Machine "KVM" changes have landed for the Linux 7.3 merge window that is wrapping up later today.
The KVM code for this next version of the Linux kernel is mostly seeing bug fixes and code clean-ups with not much in the way of user-facing new features or direct improvements.
Most notable on the KVM side for Linux 7.3, the "KVM chainsaw" code was merged for splitting up one of the god data structures. The kvm_mmu code is now cleaned up for better handling modern KVM usage. There was also other "spring (summer) cleaning" to the KVM x86 code.
The AMD KVM code for Linux 7.3 now allocates full pages for SEV/SEV-ES ENCRYPT/DECRYPT ops to fix a data corruption issue due to the AMD PSP driver assigning to-be-written pages to firmware. This Linux kernel change aligns properly now with the AMD SEV-SNP specifications. The AMD SEV-SNP population ioctls have also been hardened against bad input, among other improvements for AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization.
The Intel KVM code has also seen a number of fixes such as for servicing local TLB flushes on failed nested VM-Enter, which fixes a condition where KVM could miss a TLB on a future successful VM-Enter having the same L2 VPID. There is also a fix for VPID virtualization bugs where KVM would fail to flush hardware TLBs.
Meanwhile KVM on RISC-V added Svadu/Zicfiss/Zicfilp FWFT support for guests and optimized HFENCE request handling for SMP guests. LoongArch and ARM for KVM with Linux 7.3 is mostly about bug fixing.
More details on the Linux 7.3 KVM changes via this pull request.

title_en: Linux 7.3 Introduces 8250_mxpcie Driver For Moxa PCIe Multi-Port Serial Boards
title_pt: Linux 7.3 apresenta driver 8250_mxpcie para placas seriais Moxa PCIe multiportas
summary_en: The TTY/Serial code changes for Linux 7.3 were merged this week and include dropping the dated IPWireless driver while introducing the new 8250_mxpcie driver...
summary_pt: The TTY/Serial code changes for Linux 7.3 were merged this week and include dropping the dated IPWireless driver while introducing the new 8250_mxpcie driver...
content_en:
Linux 7.3 Introduces 8250_mxpcie Driver For Moxa PCIe Multi-Port Serial Boards
The TTY/Serial code changes for Linux 7.3 were merged this week and include dropping the dated IPWireless driver while introducing the new 8250_mxpcie driver.
The new 8250_mxpcie driver is splitting out existing functionality of the 8250_pci driver so that Moxa PCIe multiport serial board support is now found in its own dedicated driver. In turn the 8250_mxpcie driver is extended to support new MUEx50-specific UART features not found in earlier hardware. There is FIFO trigger levels, automatic hardware and software flow control, interface mode switching, and other features with these newer Moxa PCIe multi-port serial adapters.
While the 8250_mxpcie driver is added, the TTY/Serial pull for Linux 7.3 goes ahead and removes the IPWireless driver. The IPWireless driver was used for supporting some IPWireless branded 3G UMTS PCMCIA cards that were found in the US and some European countries. There's been no indications of active use since ~2011 and the likelihood of anyone still using the hardware is deemed "too low to justify continuing to carry the driver in the kernel." If there does happen to be any users left, the driver is simple enough it could be built as an external kernel module.
The TTY code also adds VT mode validation to the vt_setactive function. Until now users could pass invalid modes for the virtual terminal and end up causing undefined VT switching behavior.
The full list of TTY/Serial changes for Linux 7.3 can be found via this pull request that is already merged to Git.

title_en: Linux 7.3 Features Many Exciting Improvements, New Hardware Support & Faster Btrfs
title_pt: Linux 7.3 Features Many Exciting Improvements, New Hardware Support & Faster Btrfs
summary_en: With Linux 7.3-rc1 released to cap off the two week merge window, here is a look at the many exciting changes merged for the Linux 7.3 kernel that is working its way toward release in the second half of October.
summary_pt: With Linux 7.3-rc1 released to cap off the two week merge window, here is a look at the many exciting changes merged for the Linux 7.3 kernel that is working its way toward release in the second half of October.
content_en:
Linux 7.3 Features Many Exciting Improvements, New Hardware Support & Faster Btrfs
With Linux 7.3-rc1 released to cap off the two week merge window, here is a look at the many exciting changes merged for the Linux 7.3 kernel that is working its way toward release in the second half of October.
Among the many changes in Linux 7.3 are introducing the new Ryzen AI Halo LED/RGB driver, AMD Zen 6 enablement continues especially on the Ryzen client side, KSMBD compatibility with Apple Time Machine backups, Lenovo ThinkPad USB-C Security feature is now supported by its ACPI driver, initial kernel driver support for the 2026 Steam Controller, Intel Xe3P Nova Lake integrated graphics are now considered stable / enabled-by-default, merging FailFS, and better gaming performance for systems with limited amounts of vRAM. Plus a lot more as disclosed in the rest of the article.
On the performance side are many nice optimizations in different areas. My Linux 7.3 kernel testing remains ongoing while so far have seen very nice Btrfs performance improvements on Linux 7.3 compared to Linux 7.2 and prior. More Linux 7.3 kernel benchmarking is ongoing at Phoronix.
As noted by Linus Torvalds in the Linux 7.3-rc1 release announcement and the trend of the past number of kernels, this kernel version is on the heavier side in part due to the increased patch churn of AI/LLM coding agents both in uncovering countless kernel bugs and also assisting in the creation of new Linux kernel patches. The Linux 7.3 kernel source tree right now is just shy of 41 million lines. There has also been continued code removal of obsolete, unmaintained drivers from the Linux 7.3 kernel as a result of continued noise from the AI/LLM activity.
Processors + Memory:
- Identifying the new AMD low-power CPU core type as well as more unified Intel/AMD CPU core type handling.
- An SMP improvement to help reduce latency and better real-time performance.
- A variety of Intel and AMD power management improvements like Intel directed package-level thermal interrupts.
- A minor optimization for old AMD Athlon XP era systems that have SSE but not SSE2.
- The AMD platform drivers have been preparing for next-gen Zen 6 platforms.
- The AMD k10temp driver adds EPYC Zen 5 per-CCD temperature monitoring.
- x86/mm improvements to greatly improve the performance of latency-sensitive workloads.
- Two very exciting memory management optimizations.
- Initial preparations for Intel Starfire as that Panther Lake derived SoC for extreme environments.
- Support for several newer RISC-V extensions.
- Qualcomm Shikra SoC support has begun appearing in mainline.
- Initial support for Apple M3 Pro / Max / Ultra support but not yet GPU support or other key functionality needed for day-to-day usage.
- A power optimization for M1 Pro / Max / Ultra SoCs.
- Other new ARM and RISC-V hardware support.
- Linux scheduler improvements that can help with hybrid CPUs.
- Scheduler work that can help improve gaming performance on dated computer hardware.
- Initial enablement for IBM Power12 has begun and Linux 7.3 PowerPC begins supporting in-kernel Rust code.
- The ARM64 BBML3 feature is now supported by the mainline kernel.
Graphics:
- Improvements to Linux graphics/gaming performance for systems with little vRAM (especially ~8GB vRAM) configurations.
- DRM format modifier support for old AMD GPUs as another enhancement courtesy of Valve's Linux graphics team.
- Also for older AMD GPU hardware is improved GPU reset recovery.
- Various new AMD GPU graphics IP support like the DCN 6.0 display block.
- Nouveau now has NVDEC interface support needed by NVK for supporting Vulkan Video acceleration with Mesa 26.3.
- Various other graphics/display driver improvements.
- Over on the FBDEV side for the old frame-buffer device drivers is improvements for vintage Atari computers and Voodoo 3 / 4 / 5 graphics cards.
Linux Storage / File-Systems:
- Btrfs performance improvements that I have also shown in some of my early testing of Linux 7.3.
- Addressing a bottleneck for small I/O on PCIe Gen5 NVMe SSDs.

Linux Kernel Patches Out For Review To Enable USB4/Thunderbolt For Apple M1 / M2 / M3
There is a set of 19 patches out for review on the Linux kernel mailing list that would finally allow the mainline kernel running on Apple Silicon M1 / M2 / M3 SoCs to enjoy USB4/Thunderbolt support.
While the downstream Asahi Linux code has been carrying the USB4/Thunderbolt enablement patches, they still are working their way into the upstream Linux kernel. On Sunday was the patch series posting by prominent Apple Silicon Linux developer Sven Peter for bringing up USB4/Thunderbolt across M1 / M2 / M3 as the Apple M-series SoCs currently supported by the mainline Linux kernel.
It's taken quite a while in getting the Apple Silicon USB4/Thunderbolt support brought-up given complexities with its design:
"Each USB4 capable Type-C port comes with an ACIO ("Apple Converged I/O") block which contains a Cortex-M3 co-processor and the hardware implementing the USB4 router.
There are some caveats with the USB4/Thunderbolt support for Apple Silicon on Linux right now including the lack of suspend support as well as no PCIe or DisplayPort tunneling yet and in need of further reverse engineering:
"The main driver powers up ACIO, boots the co-processor, populates the DART and NHI children once their MMIO regions are accessible and registers the NHI with the software connection manager. The last three patches add the device tree nodes for the M1 and M2. M3 nodes will follow once the rest of the stack is upstream, but the current Thunderbolt/USB4 code has already been successfully tested on those.
For those interested in this support it can be found out for review on the Linux kernel mailing list.

content_en:
New Linux Patches Tune AMD Ryzen Zen 6 To Optimize Performance & Power Consumption
Ahead of the next-generation AMD Ryzen Zen 6 client processors debuting, an important patch series was posted overnight to the Linux kernel mailing list. These patches provide new Zen 6 client Energy Performance Preference "EPP" tunings that are important for optimizing performance and power consumption for these upcoming AMD Zen 6 desktop and laptop processors.
It turns out the upcoming Zen 6 client platforms are utilizing ACPI Energy Performance Preference (EPP) differently than existing generations of Ryzen hardware. The patches are adding new infrastructure to the AMD P-State driver for handling new tuning values for Zen 6 processors to ensure Linux will have optimized performance and power consumption.
One of the patches out today reworks the AMD P-State driver code to allow per-SoC and per-core type EPP tuning values for handling both the existing and upcoming AMD processors. The second patch then adds the new Zen 6 tuning values across the different core types and whether the EPP preference is on performance / balance performance / balance power / power modes.
Worth noting with these Zen 6 client tunings is that it does set values for the new AMD "Low Power" core type. Linux 7.3 added the bits for the new AMD low-power core that complements the existing performance and efficiency (dense) core types. Based on rumors/leaks and the timing of the patches it was suspected that this low-power core type would appear in at least some Zen 6 client designs. With these EPP tunings is now hard confirmation of performance, efficiency, and low-power core types for Zen 6. The patch also confirms the AMD Zen 6 client models as Family 1Ah with the models of 0x80, 0x81, 0x84, 0x85, and 0xe0. That helps reinforce some earlier Linux patches noting the model 80 processors indeed being client parts.
The patches are now out for review on the Linux kernel mailing list. As they don't fall directly under "fixes", they will likely have to wait now until the Linux 7.4 kernel cycle. In turn that will make Linux 7.4 an important target for AMD Ryzen Zen 6 platforms for achieving optimized performance and power consumption, unless these end up being back-ported or picked up by Linux distribution vendor kernels.

With Linus Torvalds remarking in the Linux 7.3-rc1 release announcement of the AMD kernel graphics driver changes for amounting around a third of the -rc1 changes due to the big AMD GPU register files for DCN 6.0 and other new IP additions, here are some fresh code stats at large.
With AMD enabling new hardware IP blocks for upcoming graphics hardware in Linux 7.3, it's helped inflate the size of the kernel. Linus noted in the 7.3-rc1 announcement, "It's also big as an actual diff, and the reason for *that* is not surprising either: this is yet another one of those releases with a big AMD GPU register dump. This time it's the AMD DCN6 register headers. They're huge. As usual. That's what you get when you dump all the hardware definitions as C header #defines. There's also the accompanying code for the new gen. All in all, that AMD GPU code and header dump accounts for about a third of the whole rc1 patch."
Curious, I ran cloc on the Linux Git tree as of v7.3-rc1...
Linux 7.3-rc1 comes in at 40.98 million lines... That's between 5,134,418 cloc-detected blank lines, some 4,912,366 lines of code comments, and 30,937,090 lines of detected code. In comparison for the Linux v7.2 state that came in at 40.42 million lines. It's safe to say that for Linux 7.4, it will be easily above 41 million lines.
For drivers/gpu/drm/amd that includes the header files, AMDGPU kernel graphics driver, the AMDKFD compute driver, and related display code and other bits it comes in at 6.52 million lines. That is excluding the classic Radeon DRM driver for pre-GCN hardware living outside that directory. So roughly 16% of the Linux kernel is now made up of the modern AMD kernel graphics driver code. Com Linus Torvalds comentando no anúncio de lançamento do Linux 7.3-rc1 sobre as alterações do driver gráfico do kernel AMD no valor de cerca de um terço das alterações -rc1 devido aos grandes arquivos de registro da GPU AMD para DCN 6.0 e outras novas adições de IP, aqui estão algumas estatísticas de código recentes em geral.
Com a AMD habilitando novos blocos IP de hardware para o próximo hardware gráfico no Linux 7.3, isso ajudou a aumentar o tamanho do kernel. Linus observou no anúncio 7.3-rc1: "Também é grande como um diff real, e a razão para * isso * também não é surpreendente: este é mais um daqueles lançamentos com um grande despejo de registro de GPU AMD. Desta vez são os cabeçalhos de registro AMD DCN6. Eles são enormes. Como sempre. Isso é o que você obtém quando despeja todas as definições de hardware como cabeçalho C #defines. Há também o código que acompanha para a nova geração. Em suma, que a AMD O código da GPU e o despejo de cabeçalho representam cerca de um terço de todo o patch rc1."
Curioso, executei cloc na árvore Linux Git a partir da v7.3-rc1...
O Linux 7.3-rc1 chega a 40,98 milhões de linhas... Isso está entre 5.134.418 linhas em branco detectadas pelo cloc, cerca de 4.912.366 linhas de comentários de código e 30.937.090 linhas de código detectado. Em comparação com o estado Linux v7.2, chegou a 40,42 milhões de linhas. É seguro dizer que para o Linux 7.4, estará facilmente acima de 41 milhões de linhas.
Para drivers/gpu/drm/amd que inclui os arquivos de cabeçalho, o driver gráfico do kernel AMDGPU, o driver de computação AMDKFD e o código de exibição relacionado e outros bits, ele chega a 6,52 milhões de linhas. Isso exclui o driver Radeon DRM clássico para hardware pré-GCN fora desse diretório. Portanto, cerca de 16% do kernel Linux agora é composto pelo código moderno do driver gráfico do kernel AMD. Com o Linux v7.2, o driver/gpu/drm/amd cloc mediu 6,35 milhões de linhas.
O kernel continua crescendo. Não é particularmente inesperado a forma como os drivers AMDGPU/AMDKFD e o kernel Linux em geral são desenvolvidos, mas pelo menos esses são os números atuais para os curiosos.

Linux 7.3-rc1 With AMD Zen 6 Additions, Better Btrfs Performance & 2026 Steam Controller
Like clockwork, the Linux 7.3 merge window has concluded after two weeks and the Linux 7.3-rc1 kernel now available for testing.
Linux 7.3-rc1 is available following a lot of new code landing for new/improved hardware support, file-system enhancements, security improvements, and a lot more. Of course, also a lot of fixes to different pieces of the Linux kernel as a result of AI/LLM-driven activity.
Linux 7.3 brings new optimizations for Intel hybrid CPUs, more enablement for upcoming AMD Zen 6 platforms, better Btrfs performance, Nouveau support for NVK Vulkan Video, kernel driver support for the 2026 Valve Steam Controller, initial M3 Ultra / Pro / Max support, new AMD graphics IP enablement, initial enabling around Intel Starfire, Intel Xe3P graphics with Nova Lake are now enabled out-of-the-box, FailFS is upstreamed, a low-latency mode for USB4STREAM, and a lot of other new functionality. Linux 7.3 also includes the gaming improvements from Valve for enhancing the experience when running on systems with very limited amounts of vRAM. Plus a number of old/obsolete hardware drivers continue to be removed due to the ongoing noise by AI/LLM agents.
Now onward to more Linux 7.3 kernel testing and performance benchmarking at Phoronix. My more exhaustive feature overview of the Linux 7.3 kernel features will be published in the next few days.
Linus Torvalds hasn't yet posted his release comments on the LKML but they are expected soon. Linux 7.3-rc1 is available via Git.

And I don't think that surprises anybody any more. It's all the same pattern we've been seeing for a while now.

There's also the accompanying code for the new gen. All in all, that AMD GPU code and header dump accounts for about a third of the whole rc1 patch.
But if you just mask out that big chunk, things look pretty normal, and this merge window didn't feel that different from most of them despite being large. content_en:
Linux 7.3 Lands More Audio Workarounds For Laptops & Other Devices
Following last week's main set of sound subsystem updates for Linux 7.3 that brought a lot of new audio hardware support, a second round of sound updates were merged this weekend ahead of today's Linux 7.3-rc1 release.
This second set of sound updates were focused on "fixes" but also include a lot of device hardware quirks to make various laptops and other audio devices now provide better sound support under Linux. There are also some new device IDs and more making for this interesting fixes pull request:
- The Logitech PRO X Wireless headset has a hot-pluggable microphone that becomes confused on Linux when the microphone is detached. There's a fix for that in Linux 7.3 plus also its minimum volume level handling for mute.
- A quirk is added for the MSI Thin A15 B7UC laptop to enable support for its internal microphone on that AMD Ryzen laptop.
- For the Intel Hades Canyon NUC from 2018 a quirk is added for the ALC700 codec. When rebooting from Windows into Linux, the ALC700 codec was unusable. With the code for Linux 7.3, it will now be properly initialized even if rebooting from Windows to Linux.
- The Creative Sound Blaster Play! 3 now has a quirk to deal with the minimum mute value.
- Fixing microphone detection for the TongFang XxAF5xxx that is also a laptop model shipped by TUXEDO Computers.
- A quirk for the SMSL USB DAC to avoid an audible pop sound during kernel module probe-time setup or when returning from runtime suspend.
- Patches to get the M-Audio Venom USB-based synthesizer to work under Linux. The MIDI usage had worked under Linux but the USB interface hadn't worked until now.
- Fixing the microphone mute LED for the HP Laptop 15-fd0039nt.
- New Realtek RT766/RT767 VA1 device IDs in the SoundWire RT766 driver.
- Additional sound handling quirks for the Lenovo Yoga Pro 9 16IAH10, Lenovo Legion Pro 7 16ARX8H, Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 15ABR8, and Alienware m18 R1 AMD.
The full list of the sound fixes merged to Linux Git via this pull request.

Linux 7.3 oferece mais soluções alternativas de áudio para laptops e outros dispositivos
Após o conjunto principal de atualizações do subsistema de som para Linux 7.3 da semana passada, que trouxe muitos novos suportes de hardware de áudio, uma segunda rodada de atualizações de som foi mesclada neste fim de semana, antes do lançamento de hoje do Linux 7.3-rc1.
Este segundo conjunto de atualizações de som foi focado em “correções”, mas também inclui muitas peculiaridades de hardware de dispositivo para fazer com que vários laptops e outros dispositivos de áudio agora forneçam melhor suporte de som no Linux. Existem também alguns novos IDs de dispositivos e muito mais para esta solicitação de pull de correções interessantes:
O fone de ouvido Logitech PRO X Wireless possui um microfone hot plug que fica confuso no Linux quando o microfone é desconectado. Há uma correção para isso no Linux 7.3, além de seu gerenciamento de nível de volume mínimo para mudo.
- Uma peculiaridade foi adicionada ao laptop MSI Thin A15 B7UC para permitir suporte para seu microfone interno no laptop AMD Ryzen.
- Para o Intel Hades Canyon NUC de 2018, foi adicionada uma peculiaridade para o codec ALC700. Ao reinicializar do Windows para o Linux, o codec ALC700 ficou inutilizável. Com o código para Linux 7.3, ele agora será inicializado corretamente mesmo se for reinicializado do Windows para o Linux.
- O jogo criativo da Sound Blaster! 3 agora tem uma peculiaridade para lidar com o valor mínimo de mudo.
- Correção de detecção de microfone para o TongFang XxAF5xxx que também é um modelo de laptop enviado pela TUXEDO Computers.
- Uma peculiaridade do SMSL USB DAC para evitar um som pop audível durante a configuração do tempo de teste do módulo do kernel ou ao retornar da suspensão do tempo de execução.
- Patches para fazer com que o sintetizador baseado em USB M-Audio Venom funcione no Linux. O uso de MIDI funcionou no Linux, mas a interface USB não funcionou até agora.
- Corrigindo o LED de mudo do microfone para o laptop HP 15-fd0039nt.
- Novos IDs de dispositivos Realtek RT766/RT767 VA1 no driver SoundWire RT766.
- Peculiaridades adicionais de manuseio de som para Lenovo Yoga Pro 9 16IAH10, Lenovo Legion Pro 7 16ARX8H, Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 15ABR8 e Alienware m18 R1 AMD.
A lista completa das correções de som mescladas ao Linux Git por meio desta solicitação pull.
